assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original forest village medieval pixel-art review board with TWO small quest-space panels. Ref only for timber-thatch, restrained olive woodland and brown/grey materials, not village map. Coarse crisp low-detail pixel clusters, orthographic top-down-oblique camera, square-axis ground, horizontal back walls and vertical posts, avoid diamond isometric. LEFT EED-D04-A bow-material flex-test shed: low sturdy wooden workbench carrying two short detached wood test strips, one visibly aged dark sample with old worm specks, one pale newer comparison strip. Simple small passive wooden bending jig with unstrung curved strip held lightly, no tensioned bowstring, arrow or weapon projectile. Floor rope line separates table from viewer approach; release direction points toward solid back wall, away from broad open side visitor lane. Sparse separate material rack, no roof support harvested or healthy tree cut. RIGHT EED-D04-B limited craft-sharing room with independent open door directly onto public path. Cloth entirely covers ONE rolled craft pattern on table; beside it small blank detachable attribution tag partly beneath opaque flap, CLOSED private cabinet and empty work stool. No legible secret plan, family tree, names, addresses or public posting. No people, machinery, magic, big stockpile, beds, text/numbers or watermark. Clear separate exits, public path outside safety line, subdued daylight. Blank scene does not imply workshop closure or signed permissions.
assets.qa: Dark aged and pale comparison strips, separate unstrung curved jig, visitor safety rope, covered pattern and closed cabinet appear. Left test area roof omitted and jig larger than requested; force direction/clearances require implementation review. Generator added EED-D04-A/B captions despite no-label request, correctly spelled IDs; informational review labels only. Attribution tag lies beside cloth rather than beneath flap, but remains blank. No secret plan, felling or permission inferred.

assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Pixel-art CHARACTER REVIEW contact sheet for original medieval forest village craftswomen. Four equal cells on flat neutral warm grey background with generous margins, no environment. Use reference image ONLY to match coarse muted game-character pixels and rustic fabric, not its scene layout or inhabitants. Exactly TWO distinct adult women, each appears twice. LEFT TWO CELLS same Sujin, an older adult bow-material craftswoman, practical muted brown-grey head wrap, earthy apron over long olive wool tunic, sturdy boots, modest tool belt with covered tool pouch. First pose neutral front three-quarter hands empty; second side three-quarter carefully holding ONE short curved detached wooden test strip at waist. RIGHT TWO CELLS same Geli, her ADULT niece and apprentice, clearly grown adult, dark braid, faded rust tunic under brown work apron, trousers and work boots; first neutral front-three-quarter, second side-three-quarter holding ONE small old-wood sample in both hands. Age/hair/outfits are original visual proposals, don't imply historical canon. No bow, arrow, sword, magic, trees, document, writing, family diagram or decorative emblem. Gentle work-focused expressions, not victory or confession. Tiny game-sprite proportional design intended around 40 logical pixels tall, coarse clustered hair and facial marks, minimal facial detail, no painted portrait shading or tiny ornate textures. Consistent scale, upper-left light, full feet visible, four separated figures, no labels or watermark. This is a pose review board, not animation or engine-ready sheet.
assets.qa: Two visually distinct adult women each shown neutral and holding a wood sample. Sujin head wrap/olive and Geli braid/rust proposals consistent enough across poses; no family records or weapons exposed. More portrait-detail and taller pixel resolution than requested tiny game sprite; no exact logical grid, animation alignment or palette verification. Physical appearance is original proposal; adult niece relation sourced.

assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing two-panel pixel-art review board with ONE small local correction only. LEFT PANEL bottom-front wooden courtyard gate is closed across the entrance. OPEN this gate fully: rotate its wooden leaf flush along the inside right-hand stone wall, leaving the FULL existing doorway gap visibly unobstructed with the stone paving continuing from sorting corridor to public exterior path. Do not widen or relocate doorway, no new door, no lock or person. Keep every other element and overall style unchanged: left sorting trays, folios, sealed ash jar, cold covered brazier behind far separating wall; right attribution room, windows, cabinet, table and both open exits all unchanged. Preserve composition, dimensions, colors, snow, pixel clusters. Do not add labels, text, new props, flame, signatures or magical effects. Gate leaf may be visible flat along wall but must not block walking gap.
assets.qa: Targeted left front gate opened successfully; clear paving now connects corridor to street. Leaf rests at right edge and does not cover doorway. Broad composition/props of both panels retained, not pixel-exact identity. Cold brazier remains covered/separated, no flame or exposed names. Prefer this v2, retain original v1. Scaled collision and legal door width not validated.

global_caveats: High-resolution pixel-style review images, not exact native sprites, palette or tile assets.
No runtime integration. Character appearances are original proposals unless explicitly sourced.
Reference images are concept style only, not official geography.
